subject: PetraPay: production throughput surge & 5xx spike — stabilization plan and exec readout
messages:
From: Andre Muller <andre@petrapay.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: petra-sre@petrapay.com
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 08:23:00 -0800
Subject: PetraPay production: spike in latency and 5xx errors since 07:50 PST

Vanessa / Marissa —

We just saw a sudden throughput drop and a spike of 5xx errors across our checkout flow beginning ~07:50 PST. Latency for the inferencing path climbed from our baseline 180ms p50 to ~1.2s and our merchant checkout saw a 9% error-rate increase (mostly 502/503). Attached is a quick snapshot from our APM and a 1-minute sample of traffic.

This is impacting live payments for ~20% of our traffic and starting to hit our SLAs. Can Redwood confirm if there were any deploys, autoscale adjustments, or model rollbacks in that window? We need an ETA for mitigation.

Andre
Head of Platform, PetraPay

Attachments: petrapay_error_snaps.png (png, 240KB)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Andre Muller <andre@petrapay.com>, petra-sre@petrapay.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, David Kim <david@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 08:35:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: PetraPay production: spike in latency and 5xx errors since 07:50 PST

Andre — thanks for the heads up and the attachments. We're standing up an executive-stakeholder war-room now. Immediate actions underway (summary):

- Marissa is leading a live investigation on the serving fleet (model kernels, batching, and autoscaler behavior).
- David is validating routing and fallbacks (confirming whether requests were routed to a high-latency variant).
- I'm pulling an exec brief and will share a 30-minute readout and customer-facing summary.

Can you confirm whether the affected customers are pinned to a specific model version or if traffic is to our hosted default model? Also, if you can share a minute-level request ID sample we can map requests into our logs.

We'll update within 20 minutes with a mitigation plan. Apologies — we'll prioritize this.

-Vanessa Ortiz
VP, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com

Subject: Re: PetraPay production: spike in latency and 5xx errors since 07:50 PST

Quick update from infra side (investigating live):

- No scheduled deploys or config changes in the 07:30–08:00 window.
- Autoscaler events show a short delay in pod spin-up on one Dedicated pool (us-west-2, pool-id: d-pool-17) between 07:46–07:52 — warmup latency increased tokenization time for several requests.
- We see a small fraction of requests were routed to a quantized model variant that has a known higher tail latency under certain sequence-length distributions. We've toggled routing to avoid that variant (rollback triggered at 08:42).
- Collecting heap traces and kernel latency histograms; attaching a preliminary timeline CSV.

Immediate mitigation actions taken:
- Forced routing away from quantized variant (deploy rollback).
- Increased minimum replicas in the affected pool to reduce cold-starts.
- Enabled stricter batching caps for long-seq requests to avoid queuing spikes.

Prelim result: error-rate dropped from 9% to 2% at 08:55 but latency p95 still elevated ~800ms. We'll continue to instrument.

-Marissa
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: timeline_20261218.csv

From: David Kim <david@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Andre Muller <andre@petrapay.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: PetraPay production: spike in latency and 5xx errors since 07:50 PST

Follow-up from routing + model team:

- Confirmed that during the surge a small routing policy change (experimental weight) sent ~6% of traffic to the quantized-low-memory variant. This variant is faster on avg but has worse tail behavior with sequences >1024 tokens; PetraPay's checkout prompts run near that distribution.
- We reverted the weight at 08:42 (Marissa's action).
- Also validated that the cache TTL for KV prefix wasn't populated for a subset of API keys due to a race during a previous cache prune at 06:10 — this increased compute per-request. We've scheduled a fix and back-populated hot keys.

Next steps / asks for PetraPay:
- Can PetraPay share the exact example request IDs (5–10) that failed so we can correlate traces end-to-end?
- Request permission to temporarily divert a small percentage of traffic to a Dedicated hot-path with stricter locality to validate improvement (will require an internal change on your side to flip a route).

I'll prepare a short exec summary for Vanessa by 09:30.

-David
Principal Engineer, Runtime

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 09:31:00 -08:00
Subject: Redwood — PetraPay immediate stabilizers and exec readout (09:30)

Lena / Andre —

Thanks for engaging quickly. Internal readout summary below and next steps we will take together. We will run a 09:30 executive 15-minute readout and then 10:15 technical bridge.

Summary of impact (what we saw):
- Incident start: ~07:50 PST on 2026-12-18.
- Symptom: latency increase (p50 180ms -> 1.2s), error-rate +9% (502/503) impacting ~20% of traffic.
- Root contributors (initial): routing weight to quantized variant + cache churn leading to additional compute per-request + a short autoscaler warmup delay in dedicated pool.

Actions taken (completed):
- Routing rollback (quantized variant) — 08:42 (Marissa).
- Increased minimum replicas in affected pool — 08:50.
- Back-populated hot keys and adjusted cache TTL — 09:00.
- Enabled conservative batching caps for long-seq requests — 09:05.

Effect: errors reduced to ~2% and p95 latency reduced to ~800ms. We expect further improvement after the Dedicated hot-path validation.

Proposed short runway (what we will do next):
1) Short A/B to divert 3–5% of traffic to a Dedicated hot-path to validate stable p95 < 300ms (requires your flip, low risk).
2) If validated, we will schedule a staged rollout with clear rollback steps and a 30-minute pre-notify window.
3) Post-incident RCA and model routing policy hardening within 48 hours.

Executive ask: please confirm whether PetraPay can toggle the route for 3–5% of checkout traffic to the dedicated hot-path at 10:00 PST. If yes, we'll run the validation at 10:15 and share real-time telemetry.

Rishi (cc) — request help on the credit/contract conversation if we need to propose short-term credits tied to customer impact.

I'll run the 09:30 readout with Andre (and your CTO if available).

-Vanessa Ortiz
VP, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com
